title: From Idea to Study Design
audience: Basic science researchers new to AI
objectives: State a specific, concrete gap in your own field.
Turn that gap into a feasible AI study design and absorb structured feedback on it.
Produce the datasheet or model card that documents the design's limits.

sections.name: Activity selector
sections.how_to_use: A horizontal radio at the top. Only the selected activity's input box is rendered.

sections.name: 1. Find the opening
sections.purpose: Name a gap worth closing and see a candidate AI approach.
sections.how_to_use: The more concrete the gap, the more useful the response. 'We don't use AI yet' produces nothing; a specific unmet prediction need produces something buildable.

sections.name: 2. Design the study
sections.purpose: Get structured feedback on the experiment's feasibility and clarity.
sections.how_to_use: Describe the question, the data, the approach, and how you would know it worked. This activity adds a markdown-formatting instruction to the prompt, so its output is organised with headers and bullets.

sections.name: 3. Make it rigorous
sections.purpose: Generate a datasheet or model card for the dataset or model at the centre of the design.
sections.how_to_use: Name or describe a public biomedical dataset or model. The output states intended use, provenance, and known limitations.

sections.name: Submitting an activity
sections.purpose: Send a draft and read the generated response.
sections.how_to_use: Type into the text area and press Submit. The response streams line by line and stays on screen if the page reruns. Requires NAVIGATOR_TOOLKIT_API_KEY; without it the input and button are disabled and a notice explains why.

chatbot_guidance: Work the three activities in order; each takes the output of the previous one.
These activities generate feedback, not verdicts. Encourage the learner to disagree with the output where they have domain knowledge it lacks.
The learner built a smaller model card in subsection 2.2. The point is the same: the artifact is what lets the next person inherit the caveats.
Responses persist on screen across reruns, so switching activities does not discard them.
